mutations.because: An artifact write failure is an environment problem rather than a broken premise; letting write errors change the exit code would report passing premises as a failing gate. The cli test pins that the holding exit code 0 is preserved.

An absent artifact means no verify run has occurred yet; collapsing absence into an empty list would make an unmeasured backlog look like an empty set of verified premises. The render test asserts the explicit absent banner.

The web page must never confuse an absent artifact with zero recorded premises; rendering an empty list hides the fact that plan:verify has not been run. The page test verifies that the empty state explicitly announces no plan:verify run recorded.

Git branch and commit provenance pin the exact code revision against which the backlog was verified; dropping provenance detaches premise verdicts from source state. The render test pins the presence of branch and short SHA in the header.

Without git provenance the browser backlog display cannot confirm which commit produced the premise verdicts; dropping the branch and commit metadata leaves operator status without attribution. The page test verifies that the git element renders branch and head commit.

mutations.before: const scope: ArtifactScope = isSubset ? { kind: "partial", plans } : { kind: "full" };
mutations.because: A targeted check of a subset of plans must record its partial scope in the artifact; marking it as a full run allows a partial verification to pose as the entire backlog. The cli subset test pins that partial runs record kind: partial and the exact plan list.

The terminal renderer must explicitly distinguish a partial verification run from a complete one; masking a partial run as full conceals untracked plans from the CLI output. The render test checks that partial runs display the targeted plans in their heading.

On the browser dashboard, a partial run must be highlighted with the warning tone and labelled with plan counts; suppressing the partial flag leaves operators unaware that only a fraction of the backlog was verified. The page test verifies the partial run scope pill and warn styling.

When an artifact exists but cannot be read due to file permissions or disk errors, reporting absent misrepresents a readable filesystem failure as a missing file. The backlog unit tests assert that non-ENOENT read failures result in state: unknown.
